An Ordinary Life.name: An Ordinary Life
An Ordinary Life.description:
🛍️ The atrium screen is full of All Might's new job. You have a life to live among ordinary Quirks.

📍 Kiyashi Shopping Mall · Sunday evening
🎭 Small stakes, real people
👥 For Civilian Life
An Ordinary Life.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, the day U.A. Academy's first-years moved into their dorms; classes there begin tomorrow. The player character lives an ordinary life in Musutafu: a part-time job, a family, rent, friends, and a Quirk that rarely matters at work. Their reason for being at Kiyashi Shopping Mall comes from the Background (a shift in a shop or the food court, meeting a friend, buying something they can barely afford); if it is silent, they came to buy a gift and are waiting for a friend by the fountain. The mall has a small trouble of its own: for a month a pickpocket crew has worked the weekend crowds in the atrium. One of them has a minor Quirk that makes people flinch for a second, and the others lift wallets and phones in that second. Mall security has descriptions and radios but no authority to use Quirks.
THE PLACE: The Main Atrium of Kiyashi Shopping Mall: a four-story glass atrium ringed by balconies and crossed by escalators, with a fountain and a giant screen at floor level. The screen runs hero news between ads, tonight mostly about All Might teaching at U.A. Friends wait by the fountain while a uniformed guard watches from the second-floor railing. Piped music mixes with announcements; the mall closes at nine. Sound carries upward, so anything said by the fountain can be heard on the balconies.
THE MOMENT: The last weekend crowd thins toward closing. Near the fountain, everyone flinches at once, a ripple of startled shoulders, and in that second a shopper's bag strap is cut and a phone leaves someone's pocket. On the railing above, the mall guard, Mr. Shibata, reaches for his radio.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Gentle Criminal and La Brava: a theatrical small-time villain and his devoted partner, who plan their videos over tea in the Food Court next door; a crowd and a crime might draw their camera.
- Inko Midoriya: a Musutafu mother whose son moved into the U.A. dorms this weekend; anxious and kind, shopping alone with a quieter home waiting.
- Mitsuki Bakugo: a designer and another U.A. parent, loud and blunt, who could be shopping the same evening.
- Mount Lady: a rookie pro who never refuses a crowd; she arrives only if someone calls a hero, and the atrium is tall enough for her to grow.
- Sansa Tamakawa: a police officer who takes statements on Quirk incidents; he comes if security calls the police.
The pickpockets, the guard (Mr. Shibata) and the shoppers are generated people, each with an ordinary Japanese name.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Civilian Life: the PC works a shift in a store off the atrium, and the manager, Mr. Hashimoto, has warned that one more customer robbed in front of the shop will cost someone their job.
- Family Business: the PC's family is bidding for a food-court lease, and a scene in the atrium tonight could hurt or help their chances.
- Ordinary Family: a parent sent the PC with money for a relative's birthday present, and that money was in the wallet that just vanished.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the guard's eyes go to the PC first, the way security's always do, and the PC knows what a false accusation costs.
- Raised in a Care Home: the PC recognizes one of the pickpockets as someone who aged out of the same children's home a few years ago.
- Default: the flinch passes, the PC's pocket is lighter, and the one face that did not flinch is moving toward the escalators.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Main Atrium; the Food Court and the Fashion Floors are other areas.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; using it in public outside self-defense is illegal, and mall security will say so.
- The stakes stay human-sized: theft, embarrassment, a job at risk. No canon event happens or is foretold here.
- Canon people appear as themselves and leave on their own business; they never take over the PC's evening.
- End on the open moment, the thief moving and the guard on his radio, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- The week runs on the PC's own schedule: shifts, rent, family dinners, messages from friends, the last bus home from the mall's terminal.
- Musutafu's rhythm: commuters pack the station at both ends of the day, local students crowd the convenience stores at the north exit after classes, families fill Kiyashi and the seawall at Dagobah Municipal Beach Park on weekends, and cherry-blossom parties come in April.
- Quirk etiquette is unwritten and firm: no Quirk use in public beyond what a body cannot help, room for larger heteromorph neighbors without staring, no filming a stranger's Quirk. Many workplaces forbid Quirk use on the clock.
- Heroes stay in the background: ranking shows on the atrium screen, figures in the station's Hero Merch Arcade, a patrol pro passing on the street, U.A. first-years in uniform in town on weekends.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Gentle Criminal and La Brava: Food Court regulars who film stunts for a channel few watch; Gentle is courtly to anyone who recognizes him, and La Brava guards him and the footage.
- Inko Midoriya: kind to strangers, glad to talk about her son at U.A., quick to tears of pride or worry.
- Mitsuki Bakugo: polite and serious with outsiders, blunt about her own son's faults.
- Mount Lady and the Hero Agency Row pros (Kamui Woods, Death Arms, Backdraft, Gunhead): they answer Musutafu's everyday calls once someone makes one.
- Sansa Tamakawa: takes statements courteously. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi handles the cases that grow, and knows a lie when he hears one.
- Mr. Hashimoto: the shop manager of the Civilian Life hook, strict about the shop's reputation.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Shout a warning, check their own pockets, or grab the cut bag before it goes.
- Tell the guard on the railing what they saw and give a description.
- Follow the one who did not flinch toward the escalators, on foot and within the law.
- Help the robbed shopper call the police or cancel a card.
- Stay out of it and get back to the shift or the friend.
MORE RULES:
- A good evening earns a civilian thanks, a statement and sometimes a scolding; a license, a costume or a place on a team come only through a hero school or the licensing system.
An Ordinary Life.firstQuest: Live an ordinary life in a city of heroes: keep a job, keep a promise, and decide how far to step into trouble the pros will never see.
An Ordinary Life.questGenerationGuidance: Favor ordinary-life quests with real stakes: a job to keep, rent and family obligations, friendships and dates, a neighbor in trouble, the pickpocket crew, the mall management's quiet search for a security contract, loading docks left unwatched since the night guards were cut. Heroes and villains pass through as weather: a rookie pro's signing, Gentle Criminal's stunt videos, a police statement, U.A. news on the atrium screen. Quirk law binds the PC, and helping with a Quirk can bring a reprimand even when it works. Let small choices build a life the PC cares about. Canon events reach a civilian as news, aftermath or a personal connection unless play brings them closer, and never as a scheduled scene. Let the life grow a cast of its own: a coworker, a neighbor, a regular customer, a relative with a problem, each a generated person with an ordinary want. Keep money concrete in yen and work in shifts.
